beats.lead: There is other DNA inside you
beats.note: Your mitochondria carry their own genome. It reads as bacterial, and it says they descend from a group called the alpha-proteobacteria.

beats.name: Lynn Sagan
beats.role: She published under her married name, before she was Lynn Margulis. More than a dozen journals turned the paper down before one took it.

beats.text: Two of them are textbooks now.
beats.note: Mitochondria were bacteria. So were the chloroplasts in plants. Both were settled by reading the DNA those organelles still carry.
She said the cell's whip-like tail came from a swallowed bacterium too. No genome has ever been found in it. It is the part nobody quotes.

beats.text: Vindicated is not the same as correct.

beats.line: The paper a dozen journals refused is now chapter one.
